title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: SAM'S BIG IDEA
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Sam Haddad, a pizza driver from Dearborn, Michigan.
At thirty-eight, he knew every porch light in town, and every dog that hated him.
Then one long night at the hospital gave him an idea.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THREE A.M.
segments.quote: How wonderful it is that nobody need wait a single moment before starting to improve the world.
segments.author: Anne Frank
lines: His dad had a heart scare. Sam sat by the bed all night.
A nurse named Bernice got them both laughing at three a.m.
Over her coffee machine hung a line from Anne Frank:
How wonderful it is that nobody need wait a single moment before starting to improve the world.
In the parking lot, Sam looked up nursing school.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BIG LAUGH
segments.quote: The great pleasure in life is doing what people say you cannot do.
segments.author: Walter Bagehot
lines: The guys at the pizza shop laughed. You? You faint at flu shots!
At home, his dad read him a line from an old English writer, Walter Bagehot:
The great pleasure in life is doing what people say you cannot do.
Sam grinned. Then this would be a lot of fun.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE FORM
segments.quote: I have learned over the years that when one's mind is made up, this diminishes fear; knowing what must be done does away with fear.
segments.author: Rosa Parks
lines: The application sat on his table for three weeks, under a pizza box.
Then, at the library, he saw a poster with words from Rosa Parks:
I have learned over the years that when one's mind is made up, this diminishes fear; knowing what must be done does away with fear.
He turned in the form that night, with a free pepperoni for the lady at the desk.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: FIFTY-EIGHT
segments.quote: I hated every minute of it. But I said to myself, suffer now, and live the rest of your life as a champion.
segments.author: Muhammad Ali
lines: He delivered until midnight, then studied bones until two.
His first big exam: fifty-eight. He almost quit.
Bernice texted him what the boxer Muhammad Ali said about training:
I hated every minute of it. But I said to myself, suffer now, and live the rest of your life as a champion.
Sam taped it inside his pizza bag and took the test again. Eighty-nine.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: ROOM TWELVE
segments.quote: We are here to add what we can to life, not to get what we can from life.
segments.author: William Osler
lines: On the hospital floor, Sam raced from room to room, checking boxes.
Mr. Kowalski in room twelve just wanted to talk about his old Mustang.
His instructor showed him a line from the Canadian doctor William Osler:
We are here to add what we can to life, not to get what we can from life.
Sam sat down for five minutes. Mr. Kowalski finally ate his lunch.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BADGE
segments.quote: Let us never consider ourselves finished nurses... we must be learning all of our lives.
segments.author: Florence Nightingale
lines: At forty, Sam pinned on his badge, on Bernice's old floor.
A nervous new nurse asked him a question. He said, I don't know. Let's find out.
Bernice handed him a card from Florence Nightingale:
Let us never consider ourselves finished nurses... we must be learning all of our lives.
Sam still takes classes. And he tips pizza drivers very well.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start now. Prove them wrong. Decide. Suffer a little. Add to life. Keep learning.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start now. Prove them wrong. Make up your mind. Suffer a little. Add to life. Keep learning.
Me, I delivered a pizza once. I ate it on the way.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
